We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) to produce target SMILES COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. Leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <= $405. We don't have price data, but we can assume typical small molecules are buyable. Need to find a template that directly gives target from simple precursors, likely an esterification of a carboxylic acid with methanol (or methyl ester). The target appears to be a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe methyl 2-oxabicyclo...). Actually structure: COC(=O) attached to a bicyclic [C@]12... with a ketone inside. So could be formed by esterification of the corresponding carboxylic acid: O=C([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)O (the acid) with methanol (CO). Both are likely buyable: the acid maybe not common. Could also be formed by transesterification from a more common ester? Another route: start from methyl 2-oxobicyclo[2.2.1]... Not sure.

We need to find a template that matches target and can be applied to simple precursors. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken: "carboxylic_acid", functional_groups_formed: "ester". Provide lists.
